title: Ferroelectricity, SSFLC, bistability and all that
author: Ingolf Dahl (Chalmers University)
paper_type: critical review / phenomenology (no simulation in the paper; qualitative physics arguments)
method_summary: A critical review of S.T. Lagerwall's usage of the terms polar/ferroelectric/bistability/SSFLC/hysteresis for surface-stabilized ferroelectric liquid crystals (SSFLC). Dahl argues the concepts are used non-rigorously and proposes an operational diagnostic to distinguish TRUE bistability (a genuine double-well free energy with two stable states separated by a barrier at zero field) from a merely nonlinear, lossy monostable material that only mimics a hysteresis loop.

headline_claim.quote: If we have two bistable states in the material, with a potential barrier between, the width of the hysteresis loop should be independent of the frequency, while a nonlinear, lossy material should have a hysteresis loop width that is approx. proportional to the frequency.
headline_claim.physical_claim: For a genuine ferroelectric double-well (two degenerate minima +/-P0 separated by a barrier), the coercive/switching field and hence the hysteresis-loop WIDTH saturates to a finite value as drive frequency -> 0 (barrier-limited, thermally-assisted switching). For a nonlinear LOSSY monostable material (single well, no barrier at E=0), the apparent loop area/width is purely dissipative and scales approximately linearly with drive frequency, vanishing as f -> 0.
headline_claim.testable_prediction: Sweep drive frequency omega over ~1.5 decades for (A) a double-well LGD potential and (B) a single-well nonlinear-lossy potential. Measure hysteresis loop width Ec(omega) = coercive field. Prediction: Ec_bistable(omega) approaches a finite plateau as omega->0 (weak omega dependence); Ec_lossy(omega) ~ proportional to omega (goes to ~0 as omega->0).

model_to_build.type: Landau-Ginzburg-Devonshire / TDGL scalar polarization order parameter
model_to_build.free_energy: F(P) = 0.5*a*P^2 + 0.25*b*P^4 + (1/6)*c*P^6 - E(t)*P  ; a<0 double-well (bistable), a>0 single-well (monostable/paraelectric-like nonlinear lossy)
model_to_build.dynamics: gamma dP/dt = -dF/dP = -(a*P + b*P^3 + c*P^5) + E(t)   (overdamped TDGL, Landau-Khalatnikov)
model_to_build.observable: P-E hysteresis loop -> coercive field Ec (loop width) and loop area, vs omega
model_to_build.provenance: Adapted from ollie_tdgl_phasefield_polar_skyrmion_kernel.py (Ollie) LGD free-energy + Landau-Khalatnikov TDGL update; reduced here to the 0D scalar polarization needed for Dahl's loop-width-vs-frequency diagnostic.

reduced_scope: 0D single-mode polarization (spatially uniform SSFLC monodomain), scalar P, deterministic overdamped dynamics + small thermal kick. This is the minimal model that resolves Dahl's diagnostic; full spatial SSFLC director field is out of scope.
success_criteria: REPLICATED if double-well Ec(omega) shows a finite low-frequency plateau AND single-well lossy Ec(omega) scales ~linearly with omega (ratio of slopes/plateaus clearly distinguishes the two regimes as Dahl predicts).
